title: Subscriber notice: triage log and customer verification brief
summary: Draft customer notice and verification checklist for the 2029-11-15 short-lived inference degradation affecting streaming responses in EU region. This doc is a compact triage log + status page wording + customer verification steps intended for CS and partner engineering to review before publish.
body:
Context:
On 2029-11-15 at ~09:12 UTC we observed an increase in tail latency and truncated streaming responses for a subset of EU-region sessions for hosted API customers. Surface symptoms: stalled chunked responses, intermittent final-token drops, and elevated retry rates from SDKs. Impact window: ~09:12–09:39 UTC for most customers, with a smaller tail of reconnections until 09:55 UTC for some long-lived sessions.

Immediate triage notes (chronological):
- 09:12 UTC: Automated alert (p50/p95/p99 spikes) -> on-call notified (INF-4318).
- 09:14 UTC: Quick correlate to regional routing logs showed sustained queue growth on a small fraction (~3–4%) of EU serving nodes.
- 09:18 UTC: Engineering applied a targeted routing shift to spare nodes while investigating kernel-level scheduling on affected hosts.
- 09:24 UTC: We saw partial recovery in throughput but a lingering class of sessions continued to experience truncated streams; suspected KV-cache eviction race during rolling kernel patch.
- 09:30 UTC: Canary rollback of the kernel patch completed; streaming success rate improved to baseline by 09:39 UTC.
- 09:55 UTC: Final reconciliation of pending rollbacks and cache warm-ups; monitoring marked incident as mitigated.

Root-cause hypothesis (short):
An interaction between a recent kernel patch (deployed in a narrow EU host pool) and our long-lived connection KV-cache eviction logic led to a race that allowed partial KV cache invalidation during active stream generation. That produced truncated streaming output for affected sessions until the routing/rollback actions terminated the race condition.

Customer-facing impact summary (for status page):
- What happened: Short-lived degradation of streaming responses in the EU region leading to truncated or stalled outputs for a subset of requests.
- When: 2029-11-15 09:12–09:39 UTC (mitigated) — limited reconnection tail until 09:55 UTC.
- Who was impacted: A small percentage of hosted API customers using streaming endpoints in EU regions; affected customers may have seen partial or missing final tokens in streamed responses.
- What we did: Shifted traffic off impacted nodes, rolled back a recent kernel patch in the affected pool, and performed cache reconciliation.
- Current status: Service operating normally in EU region. We are continuing verification and targeted replay checks to ensure full recovery.

Planned next steps for customers and CS teams (verification and reassurance):
1) Status page wording (concise):
   - Title: Short-lived streaming degradation in EU — resolved
   - Message: Between 09:12–09:39 UTC on 2029-11-15, some streaming requests in EU returned truncated outputs due to a node-level cache/routing issue. Traffic was shifted and a kernel patch was rolled back; normal service resumed by 09:39 UTC. If you continue to observe issues, please open a ticket with request ids and sample timestamps.
2) Customer verification checklist (what CS should ask customers to provide):
   - Example request_id(s) (from SDK logs) and local UTC timestamp(s).
   - If using long-lived sessions, note session start time and whether reconnects were attempted.
   - SDK version and whether streaming vs chunked polling was used.
3) Engineering follow-ups we will share with customers in the closure note:
   - A brief technical explanation of the KV-cache eviction race and kernel interaction (non-sensitive, high-level).
   - Confirmation that no user data was lost and no API tokens were exposed.
   - Timeline of mitigation steps taken and a link to the formal post-incident review once complete.

Draft closure email + statuspage blurb (concise customer language):
"Hello — on 2029-11-15 we identified and resolved a short-lived issue that caused some streaming responses in the EU region to be truncated or stall for certain requests. We shifted traffic away from the affected hosts and rolled back a recent platform kernel patch; service normalized within 30 minutes. We do not believe any user data was affected. If you continue to see truncated streaming responses, please reply with the request_id(s) and timestamps and we will prioritize investigation. A more detailed post-incident summary will follow once the review is complete. — Redwood Inference Operations"

Action items (owner + ETA):
- Engineering (Marco Silva) — complete full postmortem doc and technical RCA by 2029-11-20. Linked PRs and kernel rollbacks attached. (JIRA INF-4318)
- Runtime team (Ben Rodriguez) — run customer-requested replay tests for 5 highest-volume tenants that reported issues by 2029-11-17 and share findings.
- CS (Aisha Kapoor) — send initial closure/statuspage message to impacted customers by 2029-11-16 18:00 UTC; collect verification artifacts and escalate any persistent cases.
- Security & Compliance — confirm no PII/exposure and sign off on customer closure language by 2029-11-18.

Open questions / unknowns (notes for the RCA):
- Exact kernel scheduling edge: which microversion introduced the timing characteristic (investigating).
- Potential need for a small client-side SDK guard to retry final-token fetches in face of truncated streams (product discussion required).
- Whether similar host pools in other regions applied the kernel patch on staggered schedules (ongoing audit).

Attachments and references (for internal use):
- Incident timeline: INF-4318
- Root-cause tracking thread: Slack #inc-4318-thread (see pinned messages)
- Runtime PR referencing cache fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/762
- Confluence: https://redwood-confluence.local/pages/INC-2029-11-15-triage

Notes to CS reviewers (tone and edits):
- Keep public-facing language short and non-technical; give enough signal that we own the problem and took specific actions.
- Reserve detailed kernel/RCA specifics for the postmortem; do not include commit IDs or sensitive telemetry excerpts in the initial customer notice.
- Offer a clear ask for customers (request_id, timestamps) so engineering can target replays quickly.

Quick template edits for small customers (short SMS/email/snippet):
"We resolved a short streaming issue in EU at 09:39 UTC on 2029-11-15. If you saw truncated outputs, reply with the request ids and timestamps and we’ll investigate immediately."

Draft sign-off checklist before publish:
- [ ] Engineering confirms mitigation and stability metrics are green (Ben)
- [ ] Security confirms no data exposure (Security)
- [ ] CS drafts and approves language (Aisha)
- [ ] Legal reviews only-if-required for enterprise partners (Legal)

---
Notes: this is a working draft. Please leave inline comments in the Confluence page linked above or reply on Slack #inc-4318-thread for quick edits. If you want a split message for enterprise tenants (more detailed RCA snippet), tag me and we’ll prepare an addendum.
